definitions.gloss: ginjo sake; premium sake brewed from highly polished rice
definitions.explanation: A grade of Japanese sake made from rice that has been polished to remove at least 40% of the outer layer. Known for its fruity aroma and clean, refined flavor.

examples.japanese: {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{頼|たの}んだ→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I ordered a bottle of ginjo sake.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{華|はな}やか→華やか：06070_hanayaka⟧な⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This ginjo sake has an elegant aroma.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冷|ひ}やした→冷やす：02403_hiyasu⟧{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{相性|あいしょう}→相性：13654_aishou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜群|ばつぐん}→抜群：12783_batsugun⟧だ。

notes:
One of the special designation grades ({特定名称酒|とくていめいしょうしゅ}) of Japanese sake. ⟦{吟醸|ぎんじょう}→吟醸：25617_ginjou⟧ means 'carefully brewed,' and the classification requires a rice polishing ratio ({精米歩合|せいまいぶあい}) of 60% or less (meaning 40% or more of each grain is polished away). The extensive polishing removes proteins and fats, resulting in a lighter, more fragrant sake.

SAKE GRADES (by polishing):
- {大吟醸酒|だいぎんじょうしゅ}: daiginjo — polished to 50% or less, the most premium
- {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}: ginjo — polished to 60% or less
- {本醸造酒|ほんじょうぞうしゅ}: honjozo — polished to 70% or less
- {純米|じゅんまい}: junmai — pure rice, no added alcohol (can be combined with the above)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {純米吟醸|じゅんまいぎんじょう}: junmai ginjo — ginjo sake made only from rice, water, and koji
- ⟦{吟醸|ぎんじょう}→吟醸：25617_ginjou⟧{香|か}: ginjo aroma — the characteristic fruity scent
- {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{冷|ひ}や→冷や：28141_hiya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to drink ginjo sake chilled

CULTURAL NOTE:
{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ} is best served chilled to preserve its delicate aroma. It became popular in the 1980s and helped transform the image of sake from a rustic drink to a refined beverage.
